validated_results.title: No association between green tea and prostate cancer risk in Japanese men: the Ohsaki Cohort Study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study evaluating green tea consumption and incident prostate cancer risk in Japanese men with complete risk estimates.

sample_size.excerpt: In a prospective study of 19 561 Japanese men, green-tea intake was not associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer (110 cases), the multivariate hazard ratio for men drinking ≥5 cups compared with <1 cup per day being 0.85 (95% confidence interval 0.50–1.43, trend P =0.81).

cases.excerpt: Reference to population-based cancer registries identified 110 incident cases of prostate cancer (7 years of follow-up with 121 543 person-years).

effect_size.excerpt: We found no significant association between green-tea consumption and the risk of prostate cancer.
